newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Maize futures up, milling wheat mixed in Budapest.
newsitem.headline: Maize futures up, milling wheat mixed in Budapest.

text.p: Maize futures prices rose for all maturities on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Wednesday and traders said the rise could continue in order to restore a normal maize/wheat price ratio.
"If milling wheat does not want to come down, maize has to go higher," said Gabor Gyori of Order.
Maize futures prices rose by 60 to 400 forints per tonne for all maturities, ending between 17,850 forints for August and 19,600 for December.
Milling wheat prices rose by the daily 400 forints limit for May to end at 25,630 and by 100 forints for September to close at 22,900.
Nearby milling wheat and maize futures prices rose mainly because traders continued to close speculative positions, Gyori said.
Milling wheat opened for January and March 1998, with March 1998 ending at 26,500 forints but January remained tradeless.
He added that in the absence of domestic news traders were inclined to follow Chicago price movements in the short term.
However, the exposure of the domestic market to international trends did not amount to a threat, he said.
A newspaper report on Wednesday warned of a collapse of the domestic market due to overheated prices but Gyori said that was not the case.

"International companies take a global view and if they want to buy Hungarian wheat for August (the BCE) is the only place to do it," he said. "And if prices go down, some exports through Black Sea ports are still an option".
Total grain turnover was 361.3 million forints, or 787 contracts, with milling wheat accounting for 595 and maize for 132 contracts.
